Summary: Maintains, inspects, troubleshoots, and repairs aircraft structures, systems, engines, and components.
CredentialNotes: FAA A&P is important for civilian operators and many MRO roles; some DoD contract roles accept military technical training instead.

Summary: Installs, tests, troubleshoots, and repairs aircraft communications, navigation, electrical, and mission systems.
CredentialNotes: FCC, FAA repairman, manufacturer training, and active clearance can matter by employer and platform.

Summary: Focuses on propulsion systems, powerplant troubleshooting, inspections, removals, installations, and test-cell or field support.
CredentialNotes: A&P powerplant experience, OEM engine training, and documented military propulsion experience are useful signals.

Summary: Works on airframes, sheet metal, composite repairs, structural inspections, and corrosion control.
CredentialNotes: A&P can help; structures, sheet-metal, NDI, and depot-level repair evidence should be kept explicit.

RoleTitle: Aircraft Maintenance Quality or Production Lead
Summary: Coordinates inspection flow, quality checks, production control, and maintenance documentation across aircraft programs.
CredentialNotes: Civilian roles often value QA, CDI/CDQAR, technical inspector, maintenance control, and supervisor records.

Summary: Maintains, inspects, loads, tests, and troubleshoots aircraft weapons-release, gun, launcher, rack, and suspension systems.
CredentialNotes: Explosives safety, aircraft platform records, armament test-set experience, and active clearance are important signals; A&P may help only when the role is inside a civilian aircraft-maintenance organization.

Summary: Handles, inspects, assembles, stores, accounts for, and maintains ammunition, explosive ordnance, missiles, rockets, bombs, mines, torpedoes, and related support equipment.
CredentialNotes: Explosives safety, HAZMAT, ammunition accountability, forklift/material-handling credentials, and DoD clearance can matter by site.

Summary: Maintains shipboard gun mounts, missile launch systems, rocket or torpedo launchers, magazines, sprinklers, and ordnance support equipment.
CredentialNotes: System experience should be captured explicitly: Mk 41 VLS, Mk 45, CIWS, torpedoes, small arms, magazines, and fire-control interfaces are different employer signals.

Summary: Repairs, inspects, services, and troubleshoots small arms, crew-served weapons, towed artillery, and related mechanical weapon systems.
CredentialNotes: Factory armorer courses, depot-maintenance records, test-fire/QA experience, and technical-manual compliance are useful civilian evidence.

Summary: Manages ammunition receiving, storage, surveillance, issue, stock control, accountability, inspection, and hazardous-material handling.
CredentialNotes: Explosives safety, HAZMAT, inventory systems, QA surveillance, and ammunition handler documentation should be kept explicit.

Summary: DoD civilian ammunition-surveillance path focused on ammunition inspection, safety, reliability, lifecycle management, and explosives-safety support.
CredentialNotes: This is usually a federal civilian career path; prior ammunition surveillance, explosive safety, QA, and stockpile-management evidence matter more than OEM platform familiarity.

Summary: Tests, troubleshoots, repairs, calibrates, and supports weapon fire-control, targeting, launcher-interface, and digital artillery systems.
CredentialNotes: Electronics theory, schematic reading, test equipment, calibration, fiber-optic, laser, and secure-system experience are strong signals.

Summary: Maintains and repairs electro-optical, laser, night-vision, thermal sight, targeting, and sensor equipment tied to weapons or detection systems.
CredentialNotes: Optics handling, laser safety, alignment/calibration, electronics troubleshooting, and clearance evidence should be captured separately from generic mechanical ordnance work.

Summary: Maintains, tests, troubleshoots, and supports missile, launch, payload, guidance, checkout, and associated R&D support systems.
CredentialNotes: Clearance, nuclear surety or treaty-compliance experience, electronics test equipment, launch-system maintenance, and configuration discipline are major civilian signals.

Summary: Conducts offensive or defensive cyberspace operations, exploitation support, network operations, vulnerability analysis, and mission-focused cyber effects.
CredentialNotes: TS/SCI, polygraph, Cyber Mission Force experience, JCAC or equivalent training, scripting, and tool-development evidence are major sorting signals.

Summary: Finds, exploits, validates, and reports vulnerabilities through adversary emulation, red-team operations, and authorized penetration testing.
CredentialNotes: OSCP/GPEN/PNPT-style evidence helps commercially; cleared offensive cyber billets often value mission qualification and clearance more than public certs.

Summary: Monitors security data, triages alerts, analyzes network and endpoint events, supports incident response, and escalates threats.
CredentialNotes: Security+, CySA+, Splunk/Elastic, IDS/IPS, packet analysis, Windows/Linux, and clearance can materially change employer fit.

Summary: Proactively searches for adversary behavior across host, network, cloud, and identity telemetry using hypotheses, detections, and intelligence.
CredentialNotes: MITRE ATT&CK, SIEM/EDR, packet analysis, endpoint telemetry, scripting, and classified-network experience are key evidence.

RoleTitle: Digital Forensics and Incident Response Analyst
Summary: Investigates intrusions, analyzes endpoints and logs, preserves evidence, scopes incidents, supports containment, and writes technical findings.
CredentialNotes: GCFA/GCFE/GCIH, EDR, memory/file-system analysis, malware triage, chain of custody, and TS/SCI can matter by employer.

Summary: Analyzes malicious code, adversary tooling, exploit behavior, host artifacts, and network indicators to support detection and response.
CredentialNotes: Reverse engineering, Python, assembly, sandboxing, YARA/Sigma, and exploit-analysis evidence should be separated from generic SOC experience.

Summary: Builds and hardens secure systems, networks, cloud environments, sensors, identity controls, and defensive infrastructure.
CredentialNotes: Cloud certs, networking, Linux/Windows administration, IaC, detection engineering, and zero-trust or classified-enclave experience are important signals.

Summary: Designs, operates, secures, and troubleshoots networks, firewalls, VPNs, IDS/IPS, sensors, and enterprise communications infrastructure.
CredentialNotes: CCNA/CCNP, Security+, firewall/vendor training, packet analysis, and classified network operations are useful differentiators.

Summary: Plans, coordinates, documents, and synchronizes cyber operations, mission workflows, authorities, risk, and operational effects.
CredentialNotes: Planning billets value mission experience, briefing/writing, requirements translation, clearance, and operations-center exposure.

Summary: Secures space, satellite, RF, ground-station, and mission networks where cyber, communications, and space operations overlap.
CredentialNotes: Satellite communications, RF, ground systems, TS/SCI, network defense, and space-system mission context should be captured explicitly.
